tagline: The world's largest commercial real estate services and investment firm
hero_kpi_rationale: Resilient Revenue represents over 80% of Total Revenue and is the primary structural driver of CBRE's growth, fueled by increasing outsourcing of real estate services by major occupiers.

kpis.name: Resilient Revenue
kpis.explanation: Recurrent or stable revenues related to building management, projects, valuations, etc.
kpis.description: Resilient Revenue includes facility, project, and portfolio management, as well as other recurring services. It now represents the majority of the business and reduces exposure to real estate cycles.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by all company activities.
kpis.description: Sustained growth in 2025 driven by an improving commercial real estate environment, particularly in the United States.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by commercial real estate recovery

kpis.name: Core EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Core EBITDA is growing faster than revenue, indicating improved operational efficiency.
kpis.signal: Operating leverage expansion despite cost inflation

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin improves from 4.0% to 4.3% in 2025, driven by revenue growth outpacing cost increases.

kpis.name: GAAP Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net income under U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles.
kpis.description: GAAP Net Income increases from $968M to $1.2B in 2025, supported by revenue growth and cost management.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on fixed assets for business development.
kpis.description: CBRE deployed $2.7B in 2025, including $1.2B for the acquisition of Pearce and $468M for Industrious.
kpis.signal: Strategic M&A deployment for service expansion

kpis.name: Total Employees
kpis.description: CBRE employs approximately 100,000 people globally, enabling extensive international coverage.

kpis.name: Resilient Revenue
kpis.explanation: Stable revenues related to building management, projects, valuations, etc.
kpis.description: Resilient Revenue is growing strongly, reflecting CBRE's strategic shift toward recurring activities.
kpis.signal: Double-digit growth in recurring revenue streams

kpis.name: Transactional Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenues from property sales, leases, financing, etc.
kpis.description: After a period of slowdown, Transactional Revenue rebounds in 2025 due to renewed real estate investment activity.

risks.title: Cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: The report notes the Board of Directors and Audit Committee are responsible for overseeing cybersecurity risks, with real-time escalation for material incidents.

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The commercial real estate services sector is highly competitive, potentially affecting revenues.

risks.title: Regulation
risks.score_rationale: Regulatory requirements and legislative changes, including OECD Pillar Two, could impact operations.

risks.title: Litigation
risks.score_rationale: Ongoing litigation, particularly through the Telford reserve, presents risks of potential losses.

risks.title: Reputation
risks.score_rationale: Reputation is critical for a services firm serving real estate occupiers and investors.

risks.title: Geopolitical Risk
risks.score_rationale: High international exposure to geopolitical risks and foreign exchange fluctuations.

risks.title: Technology Dependence
risks.score_rationale: Increasing reliance on IT systems for operations and customer experience.

ai_positioning.summary: CBRE did not mention AI, artificial intelligence, or machine learning in the provided excerpts from its 10-K/20-F filings. The analysis focuses on acquisitions and financial aspects without addressing these technologies.
